checkpoints.note: On the reproducing path the handshake dispatcher sees `hsMsgHeader->handshakeType == SSL_CLIENT_HELLO` and materializes `SSLClientHelloMessage`, which is the parser object later returned to `readParsedPacket()` via `getHandshakeMessageOfType<SSLClientHelloMessage>()`.

The first vulnerability-relevant project read on the crashing path is the ClientHello parser reading the attacker-controlled session-ID length byte from the raw handshake. That byte becomes the session-id length used to locate both the cipher-suite length field and the start of the cipher-suite array.

Root cause. This guard checks only that the first 2-byte cipher-suite slot is inside `m_DataLen`; it does not include `index`, so it does not prove that the requested `index`th entry is in bounds. The staged patch adds `sizeof(uint16_t) * (index + 1)` to enforce the missing per-index extent check.

AddressSanitizer reports the crash when `getCipherSuiteID()` dereferences the unchecked `index`th 2-byte cipher-suite slot. On the witnessed path that pointer is past the valid message bytes, producing the saved heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2.
